items.originalTitle: Engineering study reshapes understanding of remotely triggered earthquakes
items.title: Engineering study reshapes understanding of remotely triggered earthquakes
items.summary: Understanding earthquake mechanisms and mitigating earthquake hazards remain a critical global challenge. For decades, seismologists have observed that seismic waves of large earthquakes can trigger seismic activity at distances of thousands of kilometers—a phenomenon known as remote (dynamic) triggering. Yet two puzzles persisted: Why do some triggered events occur long after the seismic waves have passed? And why do Rayleigh waves, which carry lower shear stresses than Love waves, appear more effective at triggering?
